chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, raised it (to the Imam).

That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) did not consider imprisonment except for three cases: a man who consumed the property of the orphan or usurped it, or a man who was entrusted with a trust and absconded with it.

key_terms.فَذَهَبَ بِهَا: Absconded with it / Took it away

ai.seo_question: What are the three specific cases for imprisonment according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a restrictive legal principle in Shia jurisprudence, limiting imprisonment to specific financial breaches rather than general punitive detention. It highlights the sanctity of the orphan's wealth and the trust (amanah) in Islamic law, reflecting the practical governance of Imam Ali (peace be upon him). This narration serves as a foundational text for distinguishing between civil debt/trust issues and criminal punishment in early Shia legal theory.
